title: Annotatio III §.V close: Paschasius nuances (faithful only; not by teeth) vs Lombard; Hucusque Otrokocsi; stop before §.VI
pass_a_gloss: Yet this is to be observed of Paschasius: that although he contends Christ’s flesh is properly said to be perpetually offered by the Priest under the species of bread and natural blood under the species of wine, he yet denies flesh and blood are perceived by any except A TRUE BELIEVER; he also denies Christ’s flesh is in any way chewed by teeth — which are indeed marvelous things, and in these he differs much from later followers of his sentence. He would contend Christ’s flesh is handled by hands and under the species of bread put into the mouth, yet NOT WORN AWAY BY TEETH. Clearly he had not yet so laboriously expounded the subtlety of a fiction then still recent, as Lombard and others after him on the fraction and attrition of Accidents alone. Thus far Otrokocsi in the said place.
pass_b_english: Paschasius quirks: flesh and blood under the species, yet received only by a true believer; not chewed by teeth — marvels that already distance him from later followers.
Hands may handle and mouth receive under bread-species, but teeth do not wear the flesh; he had not yet spun Lombard’s accident-only fraction/attrition subtlety. Hucusque Otrokocsi.
source_text: Hoc tamen observandum de Paschasio, quòd etsi propriè dici nam Christi carnem contendat perpetuò porrigi à Sacerdote sub specie panis & naturalem sanguinem sub specie vini, neget tamen ab ullo quàm A VERO FIDELI percipi carnem & sanguinem: negat etiam ullo modo dentibus vorari carnem Christi, quæ sanè mira sunt, atque in his multum differt ipse à posteris suæ sententiæ sequacibus. Contenderet manibus tractari carnem Christi, eamque sub specie panis, in os mitti, NON tamen DENTIBUS ATTERI. Scilicet, nondum ille subtilitatem figmenti tunc adhuc recentis tâm operosè edisseruit, sicut Lombardus, aliique post ipsum de Solorum Accidentium fractione & attritione. Hucusque Otrokocsi dicto loco.
